limitations: No native HOME/auth/relay files were read; authentication non-modification relies on source inspection, current-candidate synthetic credentials, the complete unchanged manifest and supplied native receipts.

The independent symlink counterexample used a reviewer-created harmless credential fixture, not the user's native auth store. It demonstrates the code path's ability to truncate a victim file; no user credentials were touched.

Claude requested Opus 5.5 1M/high; the late current-candidate readonly resume succeeded with exit 0 and actual UUID, but physical backend and effective effort are unknown. The separate 300-second timeout and HTTP failure remain recorded and are not hidden.

Current-candidate Codex Desktop read same UUID/turn/question/answer; this does not prove Desktop hot steering or active-turn control. Claude native terminal child was confirmed in canonical HOME with no config override but did not reach a readiness phase during the recorded observation.

The shared canonical-root DevFlower lease coordinates cooperating DevFlower workbench instances only; it cannot claim atomic arbitration against arbitrary unmanaged Claude CLI. Codex uses its official native writer lock.

Supplied regression totals are 959 Python, 6 host, 109 synthetic browser/HTTP plus 16 additional browser/JS/syntax/build receipts and 5 usability cases. The independent probes are separate and executed in reviewer scratch.
F1 remains CLOSED only on current-candidate source and dynamic evidence; old Task13 report was not edited or reused as approval.
